This ‘fee’ did not include anything and additionally we were expected to give extra ‘fees’ to their Sacristy and Digital team. Deeply disappointed for a Catholic Church. Strongly encourage couples to sought other parishes for their Nuptials.

featured_reviews.name: Sean Kennedy
featured_reviews.review_text:
St Vincent De Paul Church is more than a place of worship—it is a layered story of faith, time, and community, expressed through five defining pillars:

Miracles
Stories of quiet grace echo through generations—answered prayers, moments of healing, and an unspoken belief that faith here finds its way. The church carries an aura where the intangible feels deeply personal.

Heritage
Rooted in the legacy of Chuim village, its origins date back to the 1940s, evolving alongside Mumbai’s transformation while preserving its old-world soul and spiritual continuity.

Architecture
A harmonious blend of simplicity and purpose, its structure balances modern functionality with sacred calm—featuring serene interiors, soft natural light, and spaces designed for reflection.

Parishioners
The heartbeat of the church—diverse yet deeply connected. Generations of families shape its identity, carrying forward traditions with warmth, service, and collective faith.

Activities
Beyond prayer, it thrives as a hub of engagement—community outreach, youth initiatives, charitable work, and celebrations that bind people together in purpose and spirit.

featured_reviews.name: Advait Praturi
featured_reviews.review_text: I first joined this community almost 4 years ago. It's been a great journey. It's attractive for its vision. featured_reviews.name: Dennis K
featured_reviews.review_text:
I moved to Bombay from a small town 5 years ago and got connected to Avatar. My first impression of this community was; "If Bombay had a face, these guys should be it." I couldn't help but notice how such a bunch of talented young professionals, entrepreneurs, entertainment industry professionals, musicians, social workers, parents, and drifters somehow all managed to gather under one roof. Honestly, I would never expect busy Bombay folk to have the time to show up on a Sunday morning for something as tedious as church. And still, i could see how people were being drawn to this place every Sunday.
This community has challenged so many of my self-seeking world views and has continuously provided some great perspective on God's heart for me. I have forged many great friendships here that i will carry with me for the rest of my life.
I am really thankful for the effort made here to reveal the good news of Christ in a relevant way without watering down anything, but rather pushing for the truth to move forward in our lives.
One of the memories i really love about Avatar is from the time we used to hold our Sunday meetings in someone's living room and how the place smelled of freshly brewed coffee as you entered in. And then you got to drink it..
I highly recommend this place. I have personally found this is to be a great place to meet God, experience God's love and learn how to impact your world.

featured_reviews.name: Melissa Henderson
featured_reviews.review_text: I was a part of the Avatar community for 6 years. My biggest concern when moving to Mumbai from the US was about whether I would find a good church in such a huge city. I had heard about Avatar even before I got to India, and during my first week in Mumbai, one of my colleagues brought me to Avatar. As soon as the service started I felt home <3. I have not even tried any other churches till date! Avatar is a good mix of locals and expats, and they really love people well. I felt so welcome there, and they invite all with open arms! This community really became my family in Mumbai. I couldn't have stayed in Mumbai for 6 years if it wasn't for NLF, and I will never forget my time with this COMMUNITY. That is really what Avatar is. Yes, the services are great - the worship and word - and I definitely grew closer to God while I attended Avatar. But events, programs, and the building aside, they really embody Philippians 1:3-11 for me. Love you guys!

featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful Sunday service at Avatar. They come across as a real and transparent people group who inspire each other in the lifestyle of Christ. They had facilities for toddlers, and good coffee. Makes the 2 hour service experience quite comfortable.

The cross symbolically stands for the crucifixion of Jesus generally, but the crucifix symbolizes the one-truth in belief about Jesus that he suffered and died on it  for our sins.  Those unbeliving of the faith will be misled by incorrect emphasis at this Catholic church. Protestants simply use the plain cross and focus on the bible Word, as being guiding.
I pray for this church,
1 Peter 3:18 ESV
For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh but made alive in the spirit.

featured_reviews.name: Madhavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our Lady of Remedy Church in Kandivali West is a peaceful and welcoming place that holds deep spiritual significance for the local community. The church has a calm and prayerful atmosphere, making it an ideal space for reflection, worship, and inner peace, even amidst the busy surroundings of the city.

The church is well maintained and aesthetically pleasing, with a simple yet beautiful interior that helps devotees focus on prayer. The Masses are well organized, meaningful, and conducted with devotion, making them spiritually uplifting for people of all ages. The choir and liturgy add to the reverent experience, especially during feast days and special occasions.

One of the most admirable aspects of Our Lady of Remedy Church is its strong sense of community. The parish actively engages in social, educational, and charitable activities, encouraging unity and service among parishioners. The clergy and volunteers are approachable, supportive, and dedicated to guiding the faithful.

Overall, Our Lady of Remedy Church is not just a place of worship but a spiritual home for many. It stands as a symbol of faith, hope, and togetherness in Kandivali West, and is highly recommended for anyone seeking a serene and spiritually enriching experience.

As you step inside, there’s an immediate feeling of quiet reflection and comfort. The interiors are simple yet graceful, creating a spiritual atmosphere that invites prayer and contemplation. Regular masses, novenas, and festive celebrations bring the parish community together, especially during important occasions like Christmas and the annual feast.

What makes this church truly special is the warmth of the people and the welcoming environment. Whether you visit for prayer, a special ceremony, or simply to find a moment of peace, Our Lady of Remedy Church leaves you feeling spiritually uplifted and connected.

featured_reviews.name: Le écrivaine
featured_reviews.review_text:
The first worship centre in Mumbai of the Kerala-based Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church – also known as the Indian Orthodox Church. The original church was consecrated on 9th December 1951. This first church of the Malankara Orthodox Christians of Mumbai, which
celebrated the diamond jubilee in the year 2009, was elevated to the rank of Cathedral in the same year, by an His Holiness Moran Mar Baselius Marthoma Didymos I, seventh Catholicos of the East.
Like the other Kerala-based Malankara Mar Thoma Syrian Church, this is another church of the ethnic Saint Thomas Christian community, which had its origin in the evangelical activity of Thomas – an Apostle of Jesus Christ, in the 1st century. (Malankara is an historical name of modern Kerala).
All the ‘Syrian’ churches in the early days, had their liturgy in Syriac – an ancient Middle Eastern language, and acknowledged the spiritual leadership of the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch. To make it more relevant to worshippers, both churches now have their liturgy in Malayalam. (Antioch, then a city of ancient Syria, is now in south-central Turkey, near the Syrian border. This location is believed to have been the cradle of early Jewish-Gentile Christianity.)
On account of the limited space available on the plot leased from the Bombay Municipal Corporation, the cathedral itself is of modest proportions. No parking is available in the premises, or even on the roads outside. A night school is conducted in the basement.
The cathedral is not very far from Dadar station – where the Western and Central railway lines converge. So it is convenient for commuters from both the Western and Eastern suburban areas of the city. Those coming the Navi Mumbai area (by Harbour line) would have to shift at Kurla to a train on the Central Railway line.
This church is near an old landmark – the Dadar T.T. (tram terminus), which has now become obscure. There are plenty of buses – both BEST and state transport, running close by.
Another Dadar landmark is what is known today as the Portuguese Church. A Catholic church (Ossa Senhora de Salvação) was originally built at this location by the Portuguese Franciscans in 1596. But, this is quite a distance from the St. Mary's Orthodox Cathedral.
During the cotton mill era of Mumbai, Dadar was the location of the largest mills – Bombay Dyeing (Spring Mills), Gold Mohur Mills, Kohinoor Mills, Ruby Mills and Tata Mills, were in the neighbourhood.
[☞ I am a member of another Christian denomination, i.e., I'm not a member of the Malankara Mar Thoma Syrian Church.
This review is meant to ‘enlighten’ those who aren't members of this church, incl. non-Christians.]

featured_reviews.review_text:
This church isn’t just another place of worship — it’s one of the oldest in Mumbai, with origins that trace back over 400 years to the Portuguese Franciscan era. The original structure has been rebuilt multiple times, and the current building — completed in the 1970s — was redesigned by renowned architect Charles Correa, giving it a distinctive, almost modernist architectural character that sets it apart from traditional church designs. There’s even a special skylight in the baptistery designed by celebrated artist M.F. Husain, adding an artistic touch to the sacred space.

Visitors and worshippers consistently describe the church as a peaceful and reflective haven, providing a calming contrast to the busy streets outside. Many find the quiet interiors, gentle lighting, and sense of reverence deeply moving — whether they’ve come to pray or simply to sit in contemplation.

Inside during Mass, there’s often a beautiful choir and uplifting biblical artwork, which many visitors highlight as especially moving. The church’s atmosphere is welcoming to both regular parishioners and first-time visitors.

Conveniently located just a short walk from Dadar station, it’s easy to visit whether you’re a local or a traveller exploring the city’s heritage sites. The church also serves as a well-known landmark in the neighbourhood, sitting comfortably among the vibrant life of Dadar West.

Our Lady of Salvation Church is much more than a place of worship — it’s a living piece of Mumbai’s cultural and architectural history. Whether you’re drawn by its spiritual significance, curious about its design, or simply seeking a quiet moment amidst city life, it’s a highly recommended stop in Dadar.

Our Lady of Salvation Church, also known as the Portuguese Church, is a truly unique and beautiful place of worship in Dadar West. The church is exceptionally well maintained and always kept clean, providing a peaceful and serene environment for prayer and reflection.

Its modern architectural design makes it stand out among Mumbai’s churches — both striking and spiritual at the same time. Located just about a 10-minute walk from Dadar Railway Station (West), it’s easily accessible and a must-visit for anyone in the area.

Whether you’re attending Mass or simply stopping by for a quiet moment, this church offers a sense of calm amidst the busy city life. A wonderful landmark of faith and heritage in the heart of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Shyamji
featured_reviews.review_text:
I want to first thank Prince and team for the wonderful worship...👏👏
The church ⛪ is located on the 7th floor. Gate entry is from the market side.
I enjoyed the worship and was blessed by the word of God here.
Its a small church but well organised.
Languages: Hindi, English & Malayalam all mix through the prayer service. But still did not find it difficult to understand.
Church starts at 9:30 am on Sunday
Fasting prayer on Fridays.
They have other programs during the week.
I did not find parking and the entrance is a crowded vegetable market so better to walk.
Yes! it is very close to Dadar station and behind plaza theatre 🎭.
Attaching few pics and a video
